processing: Little is documented about how this cultivar is usually processed. Yunnan greens are typically fixed by pan-firing or baking, then rolled and dried.
harvest_season: Not well documented. Spring picking is the norm for Yunnan green teas.
appearance_dry: No reliable description exists for this cultivar; Yunnan greens are typically dark green, twisted strips.
appearance_liquor: Yunnan greens typically brew yellow-green and clear.
appearance_wet: Yunnan greens typically open to fairly broad green leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting notes are on record for this cultivar. Yunnan greens in general lean brisk and vegetal.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for a Yunnan green tea, not a recipe tested on this cultivar.

vintage_note: No selling pattern specific to this cultivar is documented. Green tea from Yunnan is usually sold as the current year's spring harvest and is best drunk fresh.
description:
Yunmei is the name of a tea cultivar listed for the Simao area of Pu'er in Yunnan. Little else is documented about it, and it rarely appears under its own name.

The characters 云梅 read as cloud and plum, but a name like that says nothing about flavour, so do not expect plum in the cup on that basis.

As far as the cup goes, only the general picture for Yunnan green tea applies: brisk and vegetal, happier around 80 °C than near the boil. If you meet it for sale, ask what kind of tea it was made into and where it was picked.
history: Little is documented about who selected this cultivar, when, or from what parent material. It is listed as a cultivar from Pu'er's Simao area, and nothing more can be stated with confidence.
